text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Lagardere shares soar 23 percent on Paris bourse, increasing capitalisation by three billion francs, after requoting on Thursday. The group's bid for electronics group Thomson was chosen by the government.
-- Unions divided on aftermath on yesterday's strike.
-- Businessman Vincent Bollore named chairman of Banque Rivaud and its industrial holdings, plans 600 million franc recapitalisation.
-- French individual investors eager to invest in pension funds, survey shows.
-- Thirty-five percent of civil servants participated in strike, SNCF railway union calls for more action in November.

-- Tonight at 2100 GMT, France shifts to a 10-digit telephone number system from current eight-digit scheme. Analysts estimate cost at five billion francs for France Telecom, two billion for French firms.
-- Finance Ministry consults with bankers on debt refinancing, analysts expect needs to reach 690 billion francs for 1997.
-- AOM airline chairman Alexandre Couvelaire wants to build strong company with insolvent airline Air Liberte, worries about foreign interest in Air Liberte.
-- Real estate market picks up, due to lower housing prices, lower interest rates.
-- Thomson Multimedia workers unenthusiastic about being taken over by Korea's Daewoo Electronics as part of Lagardere's bid for Thomson.
